factors.name: Variant diversity and trace entropy
factors.summary: n_variants, heterogeneity_rate_variants and the normalized EPA, trace, k-block, Lempel-Ziv and knn entropies load 0.85-0.94, while ratio_top_*_variants, ratio_most_common_variant and std_variant_occurrence load -0.79 to -0.94. Logs high on this factor spread their traces over many distinct variants instead of a few dominant ones. It is the strongest factor (28% of variance), and trace_len_min, trace_len_mode, distinct_activities_min and complexity_factor (0.75-0.84) also load here, so in this dataset more variants go together with longer short traces.

factors.name: Log size in events
factors.summary: Absolute activity occurrence statistics (0.78-0.91), n_events (0.76), the non-normalized EPA entropies (0.77-0.81), central trace length measures (0.67-0.74), average_edit_distance and lempel_ziv_complexity load positively; event_density loads -0.68. Because n_traces is constant, all of these grow with the number of events per trace, so this is a size factor (16% of variance). Several trace length measures cross-load on Factor 1 or Factor 3, and n_events and average_edit_distance are flagged as possible Heywood cases.

factors.name: Activity alphabet size and trace-length dispersion
factors.summary: n_unique_activities and the maximum and spread of distinct activities per trace load 0.92-0.96, together with trace-length dispersion (trace_len_geometric_std 0.82, trace_len_coefficient_variation 0.77, trace_len_iqr 0.77), advanced_trace_diversity and number_of_ties. trace_len_entropy (-0.84), epa_normalized_variant_entropy (-0.80) and density_dfg (-0.68) load negatively, while structure_dfg loads 0.67, consistent with larger alphabets giving sparser directly-follows graphs. The factor combines alphabet size with length dispersion, and the global block entropies and trace_len_max/std cross-load with Factors 1 and 2.

factors.name: Concentration of start and end activities
factors.summary: Central statistics of start and end activity counts load 0.81-0.97, while n_unique_start_activities, n_unique_end_activities and start_activities_std load around -0.79. With a constant number of traces, high scores mean few distinct start and end activities that each cover many traces. n_cut_vertices_dfg (0.87) and separability_ratio_dfg (0.85) load here too, so single entry and exit points go together with more cut vertices in the directly-follows graph.

factors.name: Directly-follows graph connectivity
factors.summary: Edge count, cyclomatic number, number of successions, maximum node degree and coefficient of connectivity of the DFG load 0.58-0.65. All five cross-load on Factor 1 (0.53-0.56), so this factor captures DFG connectivity beyond what variant diversity already explains (3.5% of variance). Several of these measures are reported as linearly dependent, which inflates their shared variance.

factors.name: Loops within traces
factors.summary: All loop measures of the Repetitions group load 0.61-0.88 and load little elsewhere. The factor reflects how many traces contain loops and how many and how long those loops are. n_traces_with_repetition does not join it but loads on Factor 2 (0.58).

factors.name: Dominance of one start activity
factors.summary: start_activities_variance (0.68) and start_activities_max (0.60) load here, and start_activities_std reaches 0.55 although it is assigned to Factor 4. The factor seems to capture how strongly one start activity dominates. It is small (1.8% of variance), and start_activities_variance cross-loads on Factor 4 (-0.60).

factors.name: Spread of end activity frequencies
factors.summary: Only end_activities_std (0.80) and end_activities_variance (0.79) load highly, with end_activities_max at 0.37. These are two transformations of the same quantity, so the factor (1.6% of variance) mainly reflects their redundancy. Unlike the start activities, the end activity spread forms its own factor.

factors.name: Trace comparison 'structure'
factors.summary: Carried by structure (0.71), with mean_variant_occurrence (-0.68, cross-loading equally on Factor 1) and rel_unique_end_activities (-0.41). Only the group of structure is defined (Trace comparison), so its meaning cannot be inferred beyond its name. mean_variant_occurrence sits at the communality bound (possible Heywood case), which makes this factor unreliable.

factors.name: Shape of activity frequency distribution
factors.summary: activities_kurtosis (-0.70) and activities_skewness (-0.61) load negatively, so high scores mean a less skewed, less heavy-tailed distribution of activity occurrences. Both measures also load on Factor 1 (-0.37 and -0.49), and the factor explains only 1.5% of variance.

factors.name: Weak trace-length histogram factor
factors.summary: No measure is assigned to this factor. The largest loadings are trace_len_hist9 (0.52) and trace_len_hist5, hist8 and hist3 (0.35-0.39), all of which remain unassigned for low communality. It probably reflects residual variation of single histogram bins and should not be interpreted substantively.

factors.name: Trace-length histogram bins 4 and 7
factors.summary: Only trace_len_hist4 (0.87) and trace_len_hist7 (0.83) load highly. The factor captures shared variation of two non-adjacent histogram bins, which has no obvious meaning beyond the data, and explains 1.4% of variance.

factors.name: Weak sequential-similarity factor
factors.summary: No measure is assigned to this factor. Moderate loadings come from sequentiality_ratio_dfg (0.48), similarity_rate_variants (0.39), average_affinity (0.37), separability_ratio_dfg (0.33) and n_cut_vertices_dfg (0.30), which tentatively point to sequential, mutually similar traces. sequentiality_ratio_dfg and average_affinity remain unassigned, so the factor is weak.

factors.name: Extreme trace-length histogram bins
factors.summary: trace_len_hist1 (0.89) and trace_len_hist10 (0.75) load highly, so the factor reflects how much mass lies in the lowest and highest trace-length bins. It rests on two measures and explains 1.3% of variance.

factors.name: Shape of trace-length histogram
factors.summary: trace_len_skewness_hist (0.71) and trace_len_kurtosis_hist (0.70) load here and also on Factor 3 (0.48 and 0.53). The factor describes the asymmetry and tailedness of the trace-length histogram beyond plain length dispersion, but it rests on only two measures.

factors.name: Frequency of rare activities
factors.summary: Only activities_min (0.52) is assigned, with activities_q1 (0.44) and activities_median (0.32) also loading. The factor tentatively reflects how often the least frequent activities occur. It is the weakest factor (1.2% of variance).

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO is 0.93, so the data are suitable for factor analysis. The 16 varimax factors explain 89% of the variance. Four strong factors account for about 69%: variant diversity and trace entropy (28%), log size in events (16%), activity alphabet size with trace-length dispersion (13%), and concentration of start and end activities (11%). Two moderate but coherent factors follow, DFG connectivity and loops. The remaining ten factors each explain under 2% and are mostly carried by one or two closely related measures, such as single trace-length histogram bins, std/variance pairs or skewness/kurtosis pairs. Several measures cross-load, in particular the trace length statistics between Factors 1-3 and the DFG measures between Factors 5 and 1.
caveats: The correlation matrix is singular (e.g. number_of_successions, n_edges_dfg, cyclomatic_number_dfg, activities_q3, activities_iqr; trace_len_q3 and trace_len_iqr), so results rely on clamped eigenvalues and pseudo-inverses.
n_events, mean_variant_occurrence and average_edit_distance reach the communality bound, a possible Heywood case that makes their loadings less trustworthy.
Sixteen factors were retained, and Factors 7-16 each explain under 2% of variance with mostly one or two measures, which suggests over-extraction.
Measure definitions only give the group, so interpretations rest on measure names and group descriptions, especially for structure and the histogram bins.

Nine measures stay unassigned (trace_len_hist2, hist3, hist5, hist8, hist9, end_activities_max, average_affinity, sequentiality_ratio_dfg, cyclicity_dfg), and Factors 11 and 13 have no assigned measure.
n_traces is constant in this dataset, so count-based measures mainly track events per trace, and the size factor may look different on logs with varying trace counts.
The factors reflect shared variance among these 2112 logs under an orthogonal varimax rotation and may change with other data, rotations or factor counts.
